item.text:
**7B.3 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Assessment:** mixed, leaning somewhat positive on formal separation from private interests, but not clean. The year shows several real institution-building moves in procurement, social protection, cyber governance, and POGO licensing. The main negative is that Marcos-era power remained intertwined with the Romualdez family’s political/media network, and rice-policy and regulatory space still looked vulnerable to business capture.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | [EO 52 institutionalizing the Pag-Abot Program](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_52_2024.html) | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-01-18 | Marcos formalized a cross-agency anti-poverty program with an inter-agency committee, monitoring, and standardized delivery. That is strong evidence of using bureaucracy rather than personal or family discretion for social spending. | 7B.3 |
| Positive | [EO 58 adopting the National Cybersecurity Plan 2023-2028](https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_58_2024.html) | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-04-04 | The cybersecurity plan was adopted as a whole-of-nation roadmap with stakeholder consultation and biannual reporting. This points to institutionalized rule-setting rather than ad hoc personal control. | 7B.3 |
| Positive | [New law to make procurement “at par with global best practices”](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1229520) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-07-22 | Marcos signed the New Government Procurement Act, which standardized procurement and was explicitly framed as reducing graft opportunities. This is direct evidence of separating public contracts from discretionary patronage. | 7B.3 |
| Positive | [PBBM refutes alleged loophole in EO 74, reiterates POGO ban in all forms](https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-refutes-alleged-loophole-in-eo-74-reiterates-pogo-ban-in-all-forms/) | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-11 | Marcos said POGOs and related licenses were absolutely banned, with no loophole. That is strong evidence of using licensing/regulation against a profitable sector rather than protecting it. | 7B.3, 7B.2 |
| Positive | [NEDA chief: Gov't flexible to review, change rice tariff](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1227544) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-06-24 | NEDA said the rice tariff was subject to periodic review and could be tweaked if conditions changed. This suggests policy was being managed through formal economic review rather than family or crony preference. | 7B.3, 7B.2 |
| Negative | [Philippines | Digital News Report 2024](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | The report says ABS-CBN’s TeleRadyo joined Prime Media, a company associated with the Romualdez family, and that the partnership broadened the family’s footprint in media. This is indirect but real evidence of family-linked business access in a politically sensitive sector. | 7B.3 |
| Negative | [Philippines | Digital News Report 2024](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines) | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | The same report says the government flexed regulatory power over broadcasters, including SMNI’s franchise risk and NTC suspension at the House’s behest. That shows licensing/regulation remained highly political, even if not proof of Marcos personally directing a favor. | 7B.3 |
| Negative | [Marcos, Romualdez parties forge political alliance](https://www.bworldonline.com/the-nation/2024/05/08/593686/marcos-romualdez-parties-forge-political-alliance/) | BusinessWorld Online | 2024-05-08 | Marcos’s party and cousin Martin Romualdez’s party formed a formal alliance in Malacañang for the 2025 midterms. This is evidence that the Marcos-Romualdez family network remained fused to state power and electoral strategy. | 7B.3 |
| Negative | [House panel flags collusion among rice importers amid tariff cuts](https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1239684) | Philippine News Agency | 2024-12-10 | A House panel flagged possible collusion among major rice importers even after tariff cuts. That does not prove Marcos personal benefit, but it shows a major regulatory domain remained vulnerable to business capture and rent extraction. | 7B.3 |

**Gap**
- I did not find a direct 2024 document proving Marcos personally steered a public contract to a family company.
- The strongest negative evidence is indirect: family-linked media expansion, political alliance with the Romualdez bloc, and regulatory settings that remained politically and commercially intertwined.
- The strongest positive evidence is structural: procurement, cybersecurity, POGO licensing, and social-welfare delivery were routed through formal institutions and review mechanisms rather than obvious personal/family control.
